engagement_background.objective: Drive $655K–$1.2M in hard cost savings across key indirect spend categories (transportation, packaging, merchant processing, employee benefits, etc.) within ~6 months, thereby creating $12–18 M in enterprise value and helping Christianbook stand-up a best-in-class, scalable procurement capability to support its PE owner (Nonantum) and future growth.
engagement_background.scope_summary: 8 primary indirect categories representing roughly $18 M of the $93 M annual spend are in scope (LTL/FTL freight, merchant processing fees, corrugated, packaging & shipping supplies, employee benefits, janitorial services, marketing software, and Ingram Book Group distribution). Low-spend / low-opportunity areas may be dropped and direct COGS are out of scope. Additional exploratory workstreams for advertising and IT may be added after data review.
constraints_challenges: Long-standing incumbent relationships (e.g., corrugated, Old Dominion LTL) create sensitivity to competitive bidding and change.
Supplier non-responsiveness or pushback when providing detailed line-item usage data needed for baselining.
Risk of “side conversations” between Christianbook staff and suppliers that could undermine unified negotiation strategy.
Limited internal procurement resources; Treya must do the heavy lifting while securing timely stakeholder input.
Aggressive timeline to finalize awards by mid-February 2025 to meet private-equity value-creation targets.

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12-month AP transaction file (~$93 M spend) was available; additional unit-level usage data and contracts must be gathered from suppliers and functional owners.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend categorization relied on supplier and GL descriptions; tail spend may be unmapped, and some high-spend suppliers may not supply complete historical usage data, requiring representative samples.

extraction_notes: Operating model classified as 'hybrid' because multiple functions (logistics, distribution center, IT, HR) own categories but no formal centralized procurement was referenced; Treya aims to create best-in-class processes.
Maturity assessed as 'medium' since Christianbook has contracts and long-term suppliers but lacks enterprise-wide strategic sourcing; statement about establishing best-in-class process supports this.
Data availability and quality inferred from repeated emphasis on collecting additional line-item data and the need to baseline spend.
Constraints list draws directly from 'Typical Project Challenges & Mitigation' slide and case study discussion of incumbent relationships.
